Transform Abundances to a Logarithmic Scale

transform_log.Rd

Explicitly convert the abundance assay to natural, base-2, or base-10 logarithms and update its scale metadata.

Usage

transform_log(x, base = 2)

Arguments

x

A glyexp::GlycomicSE(), glyexp::GlycoproteomicSE(), or SummarizedExperiment::SummarizedExperiment() object. Legacy glyexp_experiment objects are also supported.

base

Logarithm base: 2 (default), exp(1) for natural logarithms, or 10. These correspond to "log2", "log", and "log10" metadata.

Value

A container of the same class as x, with its abundance assay and scale metadata updated. Annotations and other metadata are preserved, and a replayable step is appended to the preprocessing pipeline.

Details

Generally, you do not need to call transform_log() in Glycoverse workflows: packages including glystats and glyvis perform the log transformations needed by their analyses or plots internally. Follow the input contract of the downstream function. In particular, scale-aware glystats functions use scale metadata, whereas glyvis plots that internally compute log2(x + 1) expect raw abundances. This is not a guarantee that every downstream function accepts pre-logged data. Use this function when explicitly stored log abundances are required, for example for export or an external analysis.

Input scale is read from metadata; absent metadata means "raw". Ordinary log inputs are converted directly between bases, without exponentiation or taking a second logarithm. Matching input and output scales leave the assay unchanged. "logx" is rejected because its original abundances cannot be recovered from scale metadata alone.

Raw abundances must be non-negative. Zeros become -Inf, and NA is preserved. Ordinary log inputs may contain finite negative or zero coordinates and -Inf (zero abundance). NaN and positive infinity are rejected on every input scale. No pseudocount or imputation is applied. If zeros represent missing measurements, use zero_to_na() and an appropriate imputation method. Some downstream methods require finite values. Logging a sparse raw assay may increase memory use because implicit zeros become -Inf.

See also

data_scales, glyclean_pipeline()

Examples

x <- SummarizedExperiment::SummarizedExperiment(
  assays = list(abundance = matrix(c(1, 2, 4, 8), nrow = 2))
)
logged <- transform_log(x)
SummarizedExperiment::assay(logged)
#>      [,1] [,2]
#> [1,]    0    2
#> [2,]    1    3
get_pipeline(logged)
#> 
#> ── <glyclean_pipeline> 1 step ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> 1. transform_log
#>    base = 2
